findings.issue: 側 in 机の側に ('beside the desk') should be read そば (near/beside), not がわ. がわ means 'side (of two opposing sides)' (右側, 向こう側) and does not fit this existence question; en/pt both translate 'beside/ao lado'.
findings.current: なにがそのつくえのがわにありますか。
findings.suggested: なにがそのつくえのそばにありますか。

findings.issue: Token 側 has reading がわ, but in 机の側に ('beside the desk') the correct reading is そば ('near/beside'). がわ ('side of a boundary') is wrong in this context.
Romaji carries the same wrong reading of 側 (gawa instead of soba) as the kana field.

The en translation adds 'you're driving', which has no counterpart in なんかいい車じゃない (nothing indicates driving), and drops the rhetorical-confirmation tone that the explanation itself teaches. The pt version renders the sentence correctly.
findings.current: That's a nice car you're driving.
findings.suggested: That's a nice car, isn't it!

findings.issue: Internal corpus-pipeline metadata leaked into the learner-facing explanation: 'The target is coverage' is meaningless to a learner ('coverage' is an internal selection category, not a grammar point).
findings.current: The target is coverage, practicing a color adjective + exclamation.
findings.suggested: The sentence practices a color adjective inside an exclamation.

findings.issue: Same internal-metadata leak as expl_en: 'O alvo é cobertura (coverage)' is pipeline jargon that means nothing to a learner.
findings.current: O alvo é cobertura (coverage), praticando adjetivo de cor + exclamação.
findings.suggested: A frase pratica um adjetivo de cor dentro de uma exclamação.

findings.issue: Pipeline metadata leaked into learner-facing text: 'the suggested focus is など' references an internal grammar-point assignment; など does not occur in the sentence at all, so the framing only confuses learners. Keep the なれ+すぎ analysis, drop the meta-frame.
findings.current: Although the suggested focus is など, it does NOT appear here: なれ is 慣れ ('habit/familiarity'), and すぎ is the excess suffix
findings.suggested: なれ is 慣れ ('habit/familiarity'), and すぎ is the excess suffix, forming なれすぎ ('excessive familiarity'); it is not the particle など

findings.issue: Same internal-metadata leak as expl_en: 'o foco sugerido ser など' is pipeline language; など não aparece na frase, so the disclaimer reads as noise to a learner.
findings.current: Apesar de o foco sugerido ser など, ele NÃO aparece aqui: なれ é 慣れ ('hábito/familiaridade'), e すぎ é o sufixo de excesso
findings.suggested: なれ é 慣れ ('hábito/familiaridade') e すぎ é o sufixo de excesso, formando なれすぎ ('familiaridade em excesso'); não é a partícula など

findings.issue: それ is rendered as 'this' in the literal translation; それ is the medial demonstrative 'that', and the natural en itself uses 'that' (lit_pt correctly uses 'isso').
findings.current: Whatever kind of person it may be, this (accusative) doing (subject) one can manage.
findings.suggested: Whatever kind of person it may be, that (accusative) doing (subject) one can manage.

findings.issue: Gloss for その pairs 'aquele(a)' with the description 'perto do ouvinte' — internally contradictory in pt-BR pedagogy: near-the-listener その maps to 'esse(a)'; 'aquele' is the あの (far from both) slot.
Role string leads with Japanese jargon 代名詞 instead of the pt-BR term; every other role in the batch is pt-first with Japanese optionally in parentheses (e.g. 'adjetivo determinante (連体詞)').
